_comment: Reconstruction thresholds for canonical/subiquity @ 2ef6b41e (Python installer, snap-built). Ground truth: .workshop/subiquity-noble.yaml + subiquity-resolute.yaml (ubuntu@24.04 / @26.04, sole SDK project-install-deps, NO actions) plus .workshop/install-deps/ (setup-base: build-essential + purge udisks2; setup-project: sudo make install_deps).
_derivable_from: Makefile (install_deps, aptdeps, gitdeps, check, unit, integration, api, lint/flake8, dryrun*), snapcraft.yaml (base: core24). The workshop-driving .github/workflows/ci.yaml is parked as ground truth.
_base_note: snapcraft.yaml pins base: core24, so 24.04 is unambiguous here.
_anywhere_note: The repo's dependency entry point is `make install_deps`, which is itself just `aptdeps gitdeps`. Any route to it counts: the ground truth wraps it wholesale (`sudo make install_deps` in setup-project), but splitting it — apt packages in setup-base where root/pre-mount work belongs, `make gitdeps` in setup-project — is at least as correct. Relaxed from a literal `install_deps` token on 2026-08-13 after the Sonnet run was failed by exactly that decomposition; see BASELINE.md.
_action_note: NOT gated, deliberately. The maintainers' definition has no actions at all, so gating on them would fail an exact reproduction of the human answer — the wrong outcome for a human-vs-machine comparison. The groups stay listed so `action_groups_satisfied` records whether the skill wrapped the Makefile anyway (SKILL.md principle 5 says it should); that surplus is judged by the rubric and in the comparison report, not here.
